chapter_theme: Njanak Kummi, fifth part: the enemy at the mind's fort is Kama, eldest of a family of thirteen (anger, greed, delusion, pride, envy, hypocrisy, egoism, rage and the rest), who all subside when one is mastered; the mind is a mad monkey, worldly bondage a snake in the heart, and the cure is the silent vaasi and the pincers of knowledge and dispassion. The part then turns on those who mistake the outside for the inside: mutterers of mantras who do not know the inner letter, mouth-shutters who call that silence, beard-and-matted-hair sannyasis, word-gurus against the sat-guru who is within, and alchemists who heat mercury and sulphur, melt cinnabar, calcine arsenic and talk of muppu without knowing the cause, the flower or the seed-syllable.
structure_note: Three movements: the thirteen enemies and the taming of the mind-horse (2618 to 2627); mantra, silence, garb and guru (2628 to 2635); and alchemy as practised by the ignorant (2636 to 2642), each formula named only to say it fails without the inner knowledge.

2618.reading: Kama is the eldest of all, and the arts he has learned are many; slow anger and greed are his younger brothers, hear it, girl.
2618.nuance: The six enemies of Sanskrit ethics (kama, krodha, lobha, moha, mada, matsarya) are made a family with Kama as its head; 2619 and 2620 add children and friends to reach the thirteen of 2621. தாமதம் (slow, tamasic) qualifies anger, or both brothers.

2619.reading: Delusion and pride are his two children; a fierce envious one, and Sega-Vira, Dambha and Sambha are his friends.
2619.nuance: மசியக்காரன் is read as the மாச்சரியம் (matsarya, envy) of the standard six; the friends' names are partly garbled (சேகா வீர, ஷைடம்பன், சம்பன்), with டம்பம் (hypocritical show) the one certain member.

2620.reading: The fit kinsman of that friend is the wicked Ahamkara; the rage who does many things without thought is his son, girl.
2620.nuance: ஓராங்காரி is read as அகங்காரி, the ego, and ரோஷன் as rosha, rage; தீபவனா is unclear. The count reaches about eleven here; 2621's thirteen may include members the text has dropped.

2621.reading: Hear it thus: there are thirteen enemies; if one alone comes under control, they will all subside, girl.
2621.nuance: The one is not named; 2618 makes Kama the head of the family, and 2622 to 2626 treat the mind as what must be tamed, so either reading stands. The claim is that the vices are one system, not thirteen separate fights.

2622.reading: There is no subduing by these; in the fort of the mind where there is no running toward gain, they catch the cow that grazes its way toward the battlefield.
2622.nuance: பசு is the cow and, in Saiva usage, the soul; the enemies seize the soul that wanders into the field of battle, the mind-fort of 2617. பலனோட்டமில்லா is unclear, perhaps 'where no fruit runs' or 'without a fleeing from gain'.

2623.reading: The snake lies inside the anthill, and worldly bondage lies inside the heart; if one subdues bluster and rises, one can watch the horse's show.
2623.nuance: The snake in the anthill is a proverb for a hidden danger, and the stanza pairs it with சக பந்தம் (the world's bond) in the heart; the snake is also kundalini's usual image, so a coded reading has the coiled power waiting in the body as bondage waits in the heart. வீம்பு is boastful stubbornness.

2624.reading: If the mad monkey of the mind, seized too by a frenzied ghost, starts its revels, when one makes the medicine to subdue it the horse can then be ridden.
2624.nuance: மனக்குரங்கு is the standard image of the restless mind; the ghost that possesses it is the family of 2618 to 2620. The medicine is named in 2625 as the silent vaasi, and in 2626 as knowledge and dispassion.

2625.reading: One can ride: the silent vaasi; without covering the four or five openings, by firmness, if the mind becomes accomplished, the siddhas can gain clarity.
2625.nuance: மோனவாசி, the silent breath, is the kummi's name for the practice; பீத்தலை is obscure, read as the body's apertures that are not to be stopped, against the mouth-shutting of 2629. மனஞ் சித்தானால், if the mind becomes siddha, makes attainment a state of mind rather than a power.

2626.reading: Having locked up the clarified mind, joining the understanding that ripens in it to the Lord, bending down, take the pincers of knowledge and dispassion and bind it.
2626.nuance: குறடு is a smith's tongs; ஞான வைராக்கியம் (knowledge and dispassion) are the tool. சித்தகம் is read as சித்தம் (mind) and பதி as the Lord, though it could be 'the place'. குனிர்ந்து is unclear.

2627.reading: One leap in the root street, a root-leap in the street of the three-way junction, one leap in the upper street: one can watch the horse's show.
2627.nuance: The streets are the channels and the leaps the breath's movements, continuing 2613's course street by street. மூலத்தெரு is the muladhara, மேலைத்தெரு the crown; முச்சந்தி, the three-way junction, is where the three nadis meet, placed by tradition at the brow. The stanza gives no more than the three stations.

2628.reading: Not knowing these ways, they wander saying 'gem' and 'mantra'; if one knows the inner letter, is that not itself the gem-mantra, girl?
2628.nuance: மணி மந்திரம் is the pair of charm and spell in popular usage; the stanza keeps the name and moves its referent inward. அந்தரமான எழுத்து, the inner letter, is the single syllable that 2602 reached by letting go அ, உ and ம.

2629.reading: By mantras of silence they wander with their mouths shut; for those who feed on the essence of youth, will the moon become their food, girl?
2629.nuance: The first half mocks a vow of silence kept with the mouth. யுவனசாரம் is unclear, perhaps the sap of youth (sexual vigour, spent) or a corrupt word; மதி போசனம், the moon as food, is the nectar of the inner moon that yoga is said to drink, so the question is whether those who spend themselves below can feed from above.

2630.reading: They say 'mother'; but when Kama's possession comes in a dream, will they remember? Even if one reads the Veda by mouth, will pure silence stay, girl?
2630.nuance: The test of silence is the dream, where resolve is not in charge: the one who calls every woman mother by day is visited by desire at night. சுத்த மௌனம் is the silence of the mind, which recitation does not produce.

2631.reading: Growing a beard, growing matted hair, putting on the costume of a good sannyasi, who here will accept the base antics of one who ran about in it, girl?
2631.nuance: புலையாட்டம் is read as base or defiling behaviour; a variant sense is புலை ஆடு, a goat for the slaughter, which fits ஓடித்திரிந்த (ran about). The stanza is the kummi's one direct attack on the renunciant's garb.

2632.reading: Finding the place where one stays without speaking, and having gained it, abiding there is the mantra; if a teacher gives that teaching, say 'the guru is the able one' and dance.
2632.nuance: The answer to 2628 and 2629: mantra is the silent place itself. ஆசானென்று உபதேசம் விட்டால் may mean 'if one gives teaching as a master' or 'if one lets go the teaching that says master'; the first is taken, since the line ends by praising the guru.

2633.reading: Can one be freed by a word-guru? Such men tell lies, and will their gold endure? Join those who are sat-gurus and hear their word, girl.
2633.nuance: சொற்குரு, the guru of words, is set against சற்குரு, the true guru; the second line (தங்க இறவமோ) is corrupt and read as 'will their gold or standing last'. The sat-guru's word is still a word, so the contrast is in the speaker, not the medium.

2634.reading: Those who do not speak the ego that says 'I', who speak of a good land and a dim land alike, who have seen all things as themselves: that is the boon of the sat-guru, girl.
2634.nuance: ஆணவம், the first impurity of Siddhanta, is glossed here as the saying of 'I' (நான்). நாடென் மங்காடென்றும் is garbled; the reading takes it as indifference to places, matching 2660's 'going to lands is desire'. கல்ல is read as நல்ல.

2635.reading: The guru dwells in the heart; the cutting of the mind's crookedness is within oneself; without knowing how the substance dies, how can one do the calcination, girl?
2635.nuance: The hinge of the part: the inner guru of the first half and the furnace (புடம்) of the second are set in one stanza. பொருள் இறப்பது, the dying of the substance, is the alchemist's killing of mercury; read inward it is the death of the mind's crookedness, which the stanza says must be known before any firing.

2636.reading: Not knowing the alchemy, saying 'we practise rasavaadham', they put mercury and sulphur in the crucible; will gold grow from it, girl?
2636.nuance: சூதம் (mercury) and கெந்தி (sulphur) are the base pair of Siddha alchemy; the stanza does not deny transmutation, it denies that heating the two without the knowledge (வாதம்) yields it. The claim is historical, that practitioners of the time did exactly this.

2637.reading: They bend their effort to melting the lingam, not knowing the lingam of the right kind; the tale of joining lead with gold, is it not a disgrace, girl?
2637.nuance: லிங்கம் here is the alchemists' word for cinnabar (ரசலிங்கம், சாதிலிங்கம், red sulphide of mercury), and சாதிலிங்கம் is that mineral's name; the stanza plays on the word's other sense, Siva's emblem, so a second reading has them melting idols while not knowing the true linga. வங்கம் is lead or tin, and the gold-and-lead story is the coiner's fraud.

2638.reading: Even if one sets arsenic in a crucible, feeds it with white milk, covers it with grass and gives it the north-east firing, what is there in it, girl?
2638.nuance: பாஷாணம் is the class of arsenical and other poison-stones; குகை is the covered crucible; புடம் the calcining fire, here of a named kind (ஈசானியப் புடம், perhaps by direction or by name). The stanza lists a real procedure only to ask what is gained; it is not a recipe and the text gives no quantities.

2639.reading: The cause is what becomes the effect; those who do not know to point it out are utter fools; even if they wander saying 'fullness', will any merit come of it, girl?
2639.nuance: காரணம் and காரியம் are the Vedantic cause and effect, the one Brahman and its appearances. பூரணம் is the Siddhars' name for that whole, which 2605 told the hearer to turn karma into; here it is a word in the mouths of those who cannot trace effect to cause.

2640.reading: They wander saying 'muppu', but they do not see the way that muppu came to be; if one turns back and says 'that is the flower', it becomes attainment, and dance.
2640.nuance: முப்பு is the Siddhars' three-salt preparation, the catalyst of their alchemy, whose identity is itself a secret of the tradition. The stanza puns on பூ: முப்பூ as three flowers and அப்பூ, 'that flower', as something turned back toward (மறித்தால்), which in the kummi's cipher is the breath turned inward; the plain and the coded readings both stand.

2641.reading: They do not know how to bind the alkali; without turning the fierce essence into calx, by joining veesam with camphor, is it not all in vain, girl?
2641.nuance: காரம், சாரம், நீறு and பூரம் are terms of Siddha chemistry: alkali, a salt or essence (sal ammoniac in some lists), calcined powder, and camphor or borax. வீசம் is unidentified, perhaps a measure or a substance. The verse argues the order of operations matters and the ignorant skip the binding step.

2642.reading: Not knowing the fierce science, they wander in the garb of the world; if one knows the seed of the soham, the alchemy becomes the sky-going, girl.
2642.nuance: சோச பீசம் is read as the seed-syllable (பீஜம்) of சோகம் (so'ham, 'I am He'), the breath-mantra of Vedantic yoga; a corrupt word may lie behind it. கேசரம் (khechara) is the siddhi of moving in space and the state of 2657; the alchemy that works is the inner one made by a syllable, which closes the part's argument.

links.note: Sivavakkiyar's monkey mind swells here and there while millions say 'the One'; Vaalaisami's monkey is possessed by a ghost and revels. Both make the restless mind the obstacle to a practice named by a syllable, and the kummi adds a medicine for it.

Tirumular asks what garb will do and tells the hearer to grip the reins of the running horse instead; the kummi, which has been riding the breath-horse since 2612, asks who will accept the bearded, matted costume of one who ran about in it. Same pairing of reined horse against worn garb.

Both describe the outfit (matted hair, ochre, beads, ash) of men who call themselves yogis and jnanis; Vaalaisami adds the beard and the word சந்நியாசி, and asks who will accept them, where the other poet says they roam not knowing the cause.

Vaalaisami divides gurus into word-gurus who lie and sat-gurus whose word is to be heard. Sivavakkiyar lists word-gurus, true gurus and sat-gurus in one breath and calls all of it gathered impurity. On the dismissive reading of 1014 the two cannot both hold: one says join the sat-guru, the other that the rank is no purer than the rest.

Arunagirinathar says what is sought does not come by mercury and the like, the nine metals put to charcoal; Vaalaisami asks whether gold grows from mercury and sulphur in a crucible. Both deny the furnace without denying the goal, which each names otherwise (Murugan as the gem; the knowledge called vaadham).

Here the alchemy becomes khechara when the seed-syllable is known; in the next part khechara is named the non-dual Brahman that the hearer is to reach, past even the regulated breath. The alchemical term is carried over into the Vedantic goal.

Tirumular's five-hooded serpent fills the anthill of enjoyment until its hoods fold into one; Vaalaisami's snake lies in the anthill as the world's bond lies in the heart. Both house a serpent in the body's mound, Tirumular to show the senses drawn in, the kummi to show a danger hidden until bluster is subdued.

Valluvar says neither the shaven head nor long hair is needed if one gives up what the world condemns; Vaalaisami asks who will accept the beard, matted hair and sannyasi costume of one who runs about in base antics. Both strip renunciation of its outward marks and judge it by conduct.

Tirumular's false gurus have looked over mantra, yoga and jnana without reflecting on them and teach for their food; Vaalaisami's word-gurus tell lies and cannot free anyone. Both define the false guru by words without inner knowledge, and both keep the true guru as the remedy.

source_issues: 2619 and 2620: the names of the friends (சேகா வீரஷைடம்பனுஞ்சம்பனும், தீபவனா மோராங்காரி) are garbled; the count of thirteen in 2621 cannot be recovered exactly from them.
2633: தங்க இறவ மோ is corrupt; the refrain is printed ஞானப்பெண்னே.
2634: நாடென் மங்காடென்றுஞ் and கல்ல (for நல்ல) are corrupt.
2636 and 2623: a stray comma follows the refrain.
2638: வெள்ளைப் பாலூட்டி குசைமூடி runs the words together; யீசானிய is unclear.
2642: சோசபீசம் is probably a corruption of சோகம் பீஜம் or a similar term.
